levels.title: Total Spotify Streams
levels.task: Your boss needs to know the total number of Spotify streams across the Top 50 chart. Calculate the sum and rename the column to total_spotify_streams.
levels.solution: SELECT SUM(spotify_streams) AS total_spotify_streams FROM top_songs;
levels.hintMessage: Use SUM() and give it an alias with AS.
levels.successMessage: Nice! Now your boss has the total numbers.

levels.title: Shortest Song by Artist
levels.task: In order to make a tiktok, someone on the social media team is asking about Benson Boone’s shortest song. Help find it by filtering the artist and using MIN() to find the shortest duration.
levels.solution: SELECT MIN(duration_ms) AS shortest_song FROM top_songs WHERE artist = 'Benson Boone';
levels.hintMessage: Filter with `WHERE artist = 'Benson Boone'`, then use `MIN(duration_ms)` (optionally `AS shortest_song`).
levels.successMessage: Perfect, now the team can make the tiktok.

levels.title: Song Count by Genre
levels.task: A genre specialist wants to know how many songs fall under each genre. Use COUNT() with GROUP BY, and name your new column song_count.
levels.solution: SELECT genre, COUNT(*) AS song_count FROM top_songs GROUP BY genre;
levels.hintMessage: Use GROUP BY to count rows by category.
levels.successMessage: Perfect breakdown! Now we know what genres dominate.

levels.title: Average Song Duration by Album
levels.task: Audio engineers are curious-what’s the average duration of songs per album? Use AVG() with GROUP BY.
levels.solution: SELECT album_name, AVG(duration_ms) FROM top_songs GROUP BY album_name;
levels.hintMessage: Use `AVG(duration_ms)` with `GROUP BY album_name`. Put `album_name` first in the `SELECT` list so the result columns match the expected order.
levels.successMessage: You’ve just delivered real insights for the engineers.

levels.title: Most Recent Release by Artist
levels.task: Leadership wants a list of the most recent releases by each artist. Show the artist and their latest release date, sorted with the newest songs at the top.
levels.solution: SELECT artist, MAX(release_date) AS max_release_date FROM top_songs GROUP BY artist ORDER BY max_release_date DESC;
levels.hintMessage: Use MAX() and GROUP BY, and sort with ORDER BY.
levels.successMessage: This view is super helpful for scouting new releases.
